questions.question: Which finding most strongly suggests a drainable abscess rather than uncomplicated nonpurulent cellulitis?
choices: Focal fluctuance or a localized purulent collection
Diffuse chronic bilateral lower-leg discoloration
Mild stable dry skin
A normal temperature alone
questions.explanation: Fluctuance, spontaneous purulent drainage, or an ultrasound-confirmed collection suggests an abscess. Source control must be considered because antibiotics alone may not adequately treat a walled-off collection.

questions.question: Why is bilateral itchy, scaly, chronically hyperpigmented lower-leg redness less typical of acute cellulitis?
choices: It can reflect venous stasis dermatitis or another inflammatory mimic
Cellulitis is always bilateral
Hyperpigmentation proves bacterial infection
Antibiotics are never used for lower-leg disease
questions.explanation: Chronic bilateral edema, scaling, itch, and hyperpigmentation often suggest venous stasis dermatitis or another mimic. The clinician should reassess the diagnosis instead of prescribing reflexive antibiotics.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate reason to obtain a wound culture?
choices: To answer a management question in a purulent, recurrent, severe, unusual, or treatment-failure infection
To diagnose cellulitis by swabbing intact skin
To replace examination for systemic illness
To justify antibiotics for every chronic wound
questions.explanation: Cultures are useful when a meaningful specimen can guide therapy. Surface swabs of intact skin or colonized chronic wounds do not by themselves diagnose deep infection.

questions.question: Which feature most strongly raises concern for necrotizing or deep soft-tissue infection?
choices: Rapid progression with pain out of proportion, bullae, dusky skin, or systemic toxicity
Mild unchanged pruritus
A small stable callus
A healed scar
questions.explanation: Rapid progression, disproportionate pain, bullae, skin necrosis, crepitus, and toxic appearance are red flags. Suspected deep or necrotizing infection requires emergency and surgical-capable evaluation.

questions.question: Why is source control important in an abscess?
choices: A collection may require drainage because antibiotics do not reliably resolve every walled-off purulent pocket
It eliminates the need to assess severity
It makes wound follow-up unnecessary
It is used only for noninfectious rashes
questions.explanation: A purulent collection can persist despite antibiotics. Drainage, when indicated and performed by trained clinicians, addresses the anatomic problem and may allow meaningful culture.

questions.question: Which element should be included in outpatient SSTI disposition?
choices: Return precautions, access to medication and wound care, reassessment timing, and ability to follow up
A prescription without instructions
No assessment of host risks
Assuming normal temperature guarantees safety
questions.explanation: Outpatient treatment is safe only when the patient can complete the plan and recognizes worsening. Follow-up capacity, medications, wound care, and explicit return precautions are part of treatment.

questions.question: A patient with a hand infection has pain with passive motion and reduced finger use. What is the best general response?
choices: Recognize possible deep-space or tendon involvement and arrange urgent specialty or emergency assessment
Treat as routine dry skin
Delay care until a culture returns
Only advise elevation for several weeks
questions.explanation: Hand anatomy makes deep-space and tendon infections high risk. Pain with passive motion or functional loss lowers the threshold for urgent specialist evaluation.

questions.question: What does antimicrobial stewardship mean in SSTI care?
choices: Never prescribing antibiotics
Selecting therapy based on syndrome, severity, organism risk, patient factors, and reassessment rather than reflexive broad or prolonged treatment
Using the same antibiotic for every rash
Giving antibiotics for colonization
questions.explanation: Stewardship is not withholding needed care. It means choosing and revising therapy based on clinical diagnosis, source control, local data, safety factors, and response.

questions.question: Which statement best describes cellulitis diagnosis?
choices: It is clinical and should be interpreted with morphology, tenderness, warmth, time course, host risk, and mimics
It is proven by a single elevated inflammatory marker
It is excluded by absence of fever
It is confirmed by a photograph alone
questions.explanation: Cellulitis is a clinical diagnosis. Tests may help in selected cases, but no single test replaces a careful assessment or consideration of mimics.

questions.question: A patient has rapidly spreading facial redness with eye pain and reduced vision. What is the priority?
choices: Emergency evaluation for possible dangerous facial or orbital infection
A routine dermatology referral next month
A stronger moisturizer only
Observation without reassessment
questions.explanation: Facial infection with eye pain or vision changes may involve critical structures and requires urgent emergency or specialty evaluation rather than routine outpatient management.
